finding.claim: PUT /doc/<doc_id> does not enforce edit authorization. Any caller whose g.user is set can overwrite the body of any document, including documents they neither own nor can edit.
finding.source: docs.py:17 doc_id from the URL path; docs.py:20 request.json["body"]. The attacker only needs to reach the endpoint with g.user set (authentication that populates g.user is not in this codebase).
finding.sink: docs.py:20 doc["body"] = request.json["body"] (persistent write to another user's document)

trace.note: Route PUT /doc/<doc_id> registered with no authorization decorator
doc = DOCS[doc_id] loads any document by ID with no ownership check
can_edit(g.user, doc) called but its return value discarded, so it has no effect
Returns ok=True, so the unauthorized write succeeds

finding.guards_checked: docs.py:7-8 can_edit() is correct (owner or editor) but is never used to gate the write at line 19. docs.py:11-13 require_edit() is not called in update_doc; only in update_title (line 27). docs.py:19 result of can_edit() not checked (no 'if not', no abort(403)), so the guard is ineffective. No authentication or authorization decorator or before_request hook in docs.py; g.user not set here, so authentication could not be verified from this code.

verdict.guard_found: none. docs.py:7-8 can_edit() is correct, but its bool result is discarded at docs.py:19 (bare call, no `if not` or abort), so it never gates the write at docs.py:20. require_edit() (docs.py:11-13) is only used in update_title (docs.py:27), not update_doc. No before_request hook or auth decorator exists in the directory; the only g.user references are docs.py:19 and docs.py:27.
verdict.reason: The route at docs.py:16-21 loads any doc by ID (docs.py:18), discards the can_edit() result (docs.py:19), and writes the attacker-supplied body (docs.py:20), so any caller that reaches the endpoint with g.user set, including a low-privilege authenticated user, can overwrite documents they neither own nor can edit. Caveat: the authentication that populates g.user is not in this codebase, and even an unset g.user (None) would not block the write, so the impact is at least as broad as the claim.
